facts.text: The male leaden flycatcher is a lustrous azure bird with white underparts, while the female wears a leaden head and back with a rufous throat and breast.
facts.quote: Around 15 cm (6 in) in length, the male is lustrous azure with white underparts, while the female possesses leaden head, mantle and back and rufous throat and breast.

facts.text: It catches insects on the wing, hopping actively between branches as it hunts.
facts.quote: As its name suggests, the leaden flycatcher is insectivorous. A very active and agile bird, it hops between branches and catches insects in flight.

facts.text: Around Sydney the bird is known as the frogbird, a name derived from its guttural call.
facts.quote: A local name around Sydney is frogbird, derived from its guttural call.

facts.text: The nest is a deep cup of bark strips and dry grass, woven with spider webs and decorated with lichen, placed 5-10 m up on a small branch away from the trunk.
facts.quote: The nest is a deep cup made of strips of bark and dry grass, woven together with spider webs and decorated with lichen, generally sited on a small branch well away from the trunk of a sizeable tree some 5–10 m above the ground.

facts.text: Its two or three bluish, greyish or lavender-tinted white eggs have an unusual swollen oval shape.
facts.quote: Two or three white eggs tinted bluish, greyish or lavender and splotched with dark grey-brown are laid measuring 17 mm x 14 mm. They have an unusual swollen oval shape.

facts.text: Both parents incubate the eggs and brood the chicks, though the female does slightly more and alone incubates at night.
facts.quote: Both sexes incubate the eggs and brood the chicks, although the female undertakes slightly more of the duties and also incubates at night.

facts.text: Nesting is risky business: only 23% of nests successfully fledge a chick.
facts.quote: Nesting success is low, with only 23% of nests successfully fledging a chick.

facts.text: The brush cuckoo parasitises the leaden flycatcher, laying its eggs in the flycatcher's nest.
facts.quote: The species is parasitised by the brush cuckoo (Cacomantis variolosus).

facts.text: It is highly migratory, moving from northwestern Australia across the Top End and Cape York and down the east coast to central-southern Victoria.
facts.quote: The leaden flycatcher is found from King Sound in northwestern Australia, across the Top End to Cape York, and then down the east coast to central-southern Victoria. It is rare in Tasmania. It is highly migratory within this range.
